subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations

question: Should the shipped `getAcpSessionManager()` contract intentionally stop returning an `AcpSessionManager` class instance and guarantee only the documented structural facade methods?
rationale: The isolation goal is sound, but Plugin SDK identity changes are compatibility-sensitive; tests cannot decide whether breaking class-instance semantics is an accepted public contract change.

options.title: Approve structural facade
options.body: Accept the class-identity break, document the migration contract, and land the isolated boundary before the recovery-state producer.

options.title: Require compatibility design
options.body: Pause until a safe deprecation or versioned design preserves any class semantics maintainers still support without exposing internal dependencies.

options.title: Keep recovery stack unified
options.body: Defer this prerequisite and review isolation, producer, migration, and operator behavior as one coordinated recovery change.

recommendation.title: Approve structural facade
recommendation.body: Accept the class-identity break, document the migration contract, and land the isolated boundary before the recovery-state producer.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior session API merge activity and ACP/plugin direction decisions make this the best available owner for a shipped Plugin SDK compatibility choice.
